title: SAML attribute merge ordering caused transient over-permissioning and missing audit entries
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
A high-severity customer escalation reported a case where users intermittently received higher privileges than intended during SSO login. In parallel, the audit logs did not consistently record the transient elevated role assignment, creating an investigation gap. This ticket tracks a deterministic reproduction, root cause analysis, and an urgent fix + rollout plan for RBAC v2's SAML attribute merging logic and audit emission.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure IdP with overlapping SAML group assertions: group-A -> platform-admin, group-B -> platform-developer. Enable 'merge source precedence' in SSO settings.
2) On the platform, pre-create a user with cached roles from a previous session (only platform-developer).
3) Initiate SSO login in a high-concurrency window (example: 50 parallel login flows) while an operator runs a roles reconciliation job for the user (simulates race).

4) Observe: transient assignment of platform-admin for some sessions, lasting for the duration of the login flow. Check audit log: in ~40% of reproductions the elevated assignment is NOT recorded as a role-change event.
5) Attach reproduction script and IdP assertion samples to this ticket in related_links.
root_cause: There are two interacting issues: (A) merge_ordering: when the platform reconciles SAML assertion attributes against cached platform roles, we applied a non-atomic merge that temporarily wrote combined role state to the in-memory session before validating final precedence rules. Concurrent reconciliations could observe and persist the pre-finalized elevated state. (B) audit_emission_path: audit events for role changes are emitted only on the final persistence path; transient writes performed by the reconciliation goroutine bypassed the audit emission hook due to a fast-path cache update that lacked the audit decorator.
mitigation: Immediate: 1) Added a feature-flagged server-side gate to enforce serialized reconciliation for affected customers (configurable per-tenant). 2) Enabled extra logging at WARN level for role-change paths to capture transient states and wrote a short-term workaround that rejects cache-updates if they would grant admin-equivalent roles while a reconciliation is active. This reduces risk while we deploy the full fix.
proposed_fix: 1) Make role reconciliation atomic: compute merged role set in-memory and perform a single compare-and-swap to update persisted session/role cache. 2) Centralize audit emission: move audit hook into the CAS path so any successful state transition (including transient-to-final) emits a canonical audit event. 3) Add regression tests for concurrency: high-parallel SSO assertion replays and reconciliation jobs. 4) Add a migration script that replays recent session changes for the customers who reported incidents and emits missing audit events where appropriate.
rollout_plan: Canary: runtime-1.18 cluster 'canary-a' (10% of auth traffic) for 48 hours with audit-level tracing enabled.
Monitor: custom dashboard widget for role-change rate by tenant, spike detection for admin grants, and audit-event mismatch counter. Pager alert if unexpected admin-grant rate >0.1% above baseline.
Gradual: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 5 days if canary metrics are clean. Feature flag allows per-tenant rollback immediately.
Post-deploy: run replay migration for affected tenants during a maintenance window and verify audits emitted.
Rollback: flip feature flag and revert to pre-CAS path if severe regression observed.
tests: Unit: new reconcile_atomic_test covering merge precedence semantics
Integration: end-to-end SAML assertion replay harness with parallel login flows (1000 simulated logins) verifying no transient admin state observed
E2E: smoke against Private deployment with KMS to ensure no regression in session persistence encryption
Audit: automated test that induces role-change and asserts audit event produced with correct before/after payload
